audit_findings.title: Historical owner earnings may mix fundamentally different business perimeters
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent historical business perimeters can distort the OE trend used to set the $890.9 million anchor and the apparent sustainable growth rate.
audit_findings.evidence: The Energy business, which was part of our Energy and Specialized Markets segment, was classified as discontinued operations per ASC 205-20 as we determined, qualitatively and quantitatively, that this transaction represented a strategic shift that had a major effect on our operations and financial results.
audit_findings.explanation: The Energy disposal and the valuation's null perimeter ruling are demonstrated. Whether the 2016–2020 OE observations include Energy is unresolved because the filing's recast covers only periods presented. Since five of the nine trend observations predate the disposal and the anchor is generated from that trend, the record cannot establish a comparable historical earnings base. Including Energy could raise historical OE levels but flatten the fitted growth slope, so the net value direction is unknown.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct every OE observation on the current continuing-operations perimeter, including Energy and other dispositions, then rerun the log trend, anchor selection and scenario valuation.

audit_findings.title: AccuLynx litigation could impose a major unmodeled claim or forced acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.35 billion acquisition consideration; monetary damages unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Specific performance would add an acquired business, purchase consideration and financing costs; damages or settlement would reduce the equity bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 21, 2026, AccuLynx filed counterclaims against Verisk in the declaratory judgment action, asserting that Verisk has breached the parties' Agreement and that AccuLynx is entitled to specific performance of the Agreement and/or monetary damages.
audit_findings.explanation: The counterclaim, expedited proceeding and completed June 2026 trial are demonstrated, while the outcome remains unresolved. The $2.35 billion consideration equals approximately 15.3%–21.0% of the modeled scenario equity values of $11.176–$15.346 billion, so the proceeding is plainly capable of changing the valuation conclusion. Direction is mixed because specific performance exchanges financing for an operating asset whose earnings and value are not modeled, whereas damages would directly reduce common-equity value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the final Chancery Court decision and any appeal, settlement or damages ruling; if specific performance is ordered, add AccuLynx OE, purchase accounting and financing to the model, and if damages are imposed, deduct the after-tax cash obligation from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The historical numerator may not carry the interest burden of the valuation-date debt
audit_findings.magnitude: $59.2 million pretax annualized proxy; approximately $7.40 per share at the bull valuation multiple
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher recurring net interest reduces equity-level OE because debt principal is not separately deducted in this methodology.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense, net was $170.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $124.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 , an increase of $46.3 million or 37.2% .
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: June 2026 debt was $4.4735 billion, while the anchor uses FY2025 OE. Annualized Q2 2026 net interest is $211.2 million, compared with $152.0 million for FY2025 after removing the filed $18.9 million accelerated issuance-cost charge, a $59.2 million pretax proxy difference. Even applying that entire pretax amount directly to the anchor and the bull operating-PV multiple reduces value by about $7.40 per share, versus the $70.16 gap between the $115.63 bull value and the $185.79 price. The precise recurring amount remains unresolved because quarterly net interest includes changing cash balances and financing timing, but the filed scale is insufficient to reverse the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Normalize annualized Q2 2026 interest for temporary redemption effects and cash interest, conform it to the June 2026 debt schedule, and rerun OE to document the smaller corrected value.

audit_findings.title: The December 2025 Marketing Solutions sale is missing from the perimeter ruling
audit_findings.magnitude: $80.0 million net proceeds and $18.4 million pretax sale loss; divested operating OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained Marketing Solutions operating OE would overstate the future numerator, while retaining the disposal loss would understate it; sale proceeds could also be duplicated in the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 31, 2025, we sold our Verisk Marketing Solutions business to ActiveProspect, backed by Five Elms Capital Management, LLC, for a net cash sale price of $80.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The sale, proceeds and loss are demonstrated, and FY2025 includes almost a full year of the disposed business. The valuation supplies no perimeter adjustment or business-level OE, so the continuing earnings removed by the sale cannot be compared with the $890.9 million anchor. The opposing effects of divested earnings and the nonrecurring $18.4 million loss make direction mixed, and the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Prepare after-tax Marketing Solutions OE by historical year, reverse the $18.4 million disposal loss and associated tax effects, verify whether the $80.0 million proceeds remain in June 2026 cash, and rerun the anchor and bridge.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified litigation exposures may be absent from both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.64 million claimed statutory damages before punitive damages, fees and other relief; remaining exposures unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Judgments and settlements reduce the equity bridge, while recurring remediation, compliance and legal costs reduce OE and potentially growth.
audit_findings.evidence: With respect to Ongoing Matters, we are unable, at the present time, to determine the ultimate resolution of or provide a reasonable estimate of the range of possible loss attributable to Ongoing Matters or the impact these matters may have on our results of operations, financial position, or cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The pending proceedings and inability to estimate their losses are demonstrated, but liability and recoveries remain unresolved. The Daniel's Law claim alone identifies approximately 19,640 persons seeking $1,000 per violation, or $19.64 million before punitive damages, injunction costs and fees. That amount is small relative to the $11.176–$15.346 billion scenario equity values, but the telematics, trade-secret, indemnification and other exposures have no estimable range, so aggregate materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Update each matter for rulings, claimed damages, accruals, settlements, insurance or indemnification coverage and recurring compliance costs; deduct probable after-tax claims from the bridge and normalize recurring costs in OE.

audit_findings.title: A failed-deal financing loss may have been retained as recurring interest cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $33.9 million pretax maximum identified loss, comprising $15.0 million redemption premium and $18.9 million accelerated issuance-cost amortization; maximum direct bull-value effect approximately $4.23 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Treating failed-deal financing charges as recurring depresses FY2025 OE and, through that observation, the fitted trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, we recognized a total loss of $ 33.9 million related to the redemption of the 2030 Senior Notes and 2036 Senior Notes consisting of a 1.0 % redemption premium of $15.0 million charged to "Net (loss) gain on early extinguishment of debt" and the amortization of deferred issuance costs and original issuance discounts of $18.9 million to "Interest expense, net" within the accompanying consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The $33.9 million nonrecurring loss is demonstrated; whether the OE worksheet normalized it is unresolved. Even conservatively adding the entire pretax loss directly to the $890.9 million anchor—larger than its likely effect through one trend observation—would increase bull value by about $4.23 per share to approximately $119.86, still $65.93 below the $185.79 price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 OE reconciliation and remove the $15.0 million premium and $18.9 million accelerated amortization if retained, without removing ordinary recurring interest; rerun the trend for documentation.
